predecessors.name: Despotate of Epirus
predecessors.text: Thessaly, which 'John, Michael's illegitimate son, received' when Michael II's dominions were split in 1267/8

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: 'Most of Thessaly was taken by the Byzantines following a campaign by Andronikos III Paleologos' (1332); the Byzantines 'established direct control over the northern and eastern part of the region'

successors.name: Despotate of Epirus
successors.text: western Thessaly: John II Orsini of Epirus invaded after Gabrielopoulos' death; per Ferjancic 'the western part remained under Epirote rule until Orsini's death three years later' (Medieval Thessaly…

rulers.name: Constantine Doukas and Theodore Doukas
rulers.title: joint rulers, sons of John I

rulers.name: Stephen Gabrielopoulos
rulers.title: sebastokrator, de facto governor of much of Thessaly for the Byzantine emperor

ledger.x: 1268: John I Doukas takes Thessaly at the partition of Michael II's dominions.
1318: John II Doukas dies without a male heir and the Doukas despotate ends.
1319: the Catalan Company occupies southern Thessaly.
1319: the seat moves from Neopatras to Trikala.
1325: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa are Catalan.
1332: the Byzantines take most of Thessaly.
1332: John II Orsini of Epirus takes the west.

wars.name: Byzantine-Thessalian wars under John I Doukas
wars.outcome: No border change on the page: John I won the Battle of Neopatras with Athenian aid against an army under John Palaiologos (c.

wars.name: Thessalian invasion of Epirus
wars.outcome: 'In 1295 the brothers invaded Epirus themselves and seized Naupaktos, but no further gains appear to have been made.'

wars.name: Catalan Company raids on Thessaly
wars.outcome: The Company 'plundered Thessaly' in 1306-1310 and in 1310 'occupied a series of forts in the south' (Thessaly page); 'In early 1309 the Catalan Company ... crossed from Macedonia into Thessaly' (Medieval Thessaly).

wars.name: Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly
wars.outcome: The Catalans take Neopatras in 1319 and Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa by 1325 and form the Duchy of Neopatras.

wars.name: Byzantine and Epirote partition of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Andronikos III takes most of Thessaly (the north and east, per the Stephen page); John II Orsini of Epirus seizes the west; all Thessaly is Byzantine after Orsini's death three years later (about 1335/6).

certainty.note: Thirteenth- and fourteenth-century Thessalian frontiers are named by towns and castles only; the 1318-1332 division among magnates, Byzantines and Catalans is not delimited by any page.

sources.title: Medieval Thessaly (the page loads as 'History of Thessaly')
